statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry - MCIL Online Filing Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The approved corporate name must be expressed in Roman script. Names in non-Roman or Chinese characters are not accepted; a transliteration or English translation approved by the Registrar of International Companies is mandatory. The corporate suffix must be 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc', or an equivalent approved abbreviation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the legal and factual grounds for approval. The Registrar must issue a decision within 7 business days. If rejection is upheld, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Act 1960 within 30 days of the final administrative refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the operational delivery of UI/UX design subscription services, provided the International Company maintains a physical registered office in Samoa at the address of its licensed registered agent and appoints a resident registered agent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; Sections 5 (mode of incorporation), 8 (Memorandum and Articles of Association), 18 (registered office and registered agent), and 34 (board of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Central Bank of Samoa Building, Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 (Application for Registration of an International Company) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the International Companies Act 1987; no escrow account or capital deposit is mandated. The Company may adopt a nominal share capital of one ordinary share at US$1.00 par value, fully subscribed and paid to the subscriber, with shares denominated in any permitted currency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscriber adopts the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar of International Companies upon incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the allotment and issuance of one ordinary share at par value to the subscriber, fully paid, be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company, situated with the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, be and is hereby adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole Director and [Secretary Name] as Corporate Secretary of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the said officers be vested with authority to open bank accounts, mandate payment processors, execute contracts, and make all statutory filings with the Samoa International Finance Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the Proposed Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa; submissions made exclusively through a licensed SIFA registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-2 listing up to three proposed corporate names in English, each ending with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or 'Ltd'. Confirm that no name conflicts with any existing Samoa international company, local company, or a restricted/protected word. Upon approval, obtain the Certificate of Name Reservation, which remains valid for thirty days.
required_dossiers: Form IC-2 (Name Reservation Request)
Certified copy of the passport or corporate registry extract of the applicant/subscriber
Written instructions from the beneficial owner specifying the order of preferred names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on the grounds of similarity or prohibited wording, the registered agent may re-file with substitute names within the reservation window; the reservation fee is non-refundable but no penalty is imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscriber, notarizing officer, and the licensed SIFA registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles in English in accordance with Section 8 of the International Companies Act 1987, including the company name, registered office clause, share capital clause, director indemnity provisions, and the object of providing digital UI/UX design subscription services. Have the subscriber execute the document before a witness or notary and deliver the executed copy, together with consents, to the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Consent to act as first director(s)
Consent of the licensed registered agent
Certified identification documents of the subscriber and director (passport and proof of residential address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent or notary identifies defective clauses, the document is marked-up and returned for re-execution; only the signature page requires re-execution if the notary attests the remainder, avoiding full re-drafting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA, Central Bank of Samoa Building, Apia, Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1, the original executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered agent's statutory declaration of compliance, consents of the first directors and secretary, and proof of payment of the US$200 government filing fee. The application is reviewed under Section 5 of the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Registration of an International Company)
Two original executed copies of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent's statutory declaration of compliance
Consents of the first directors and corporate secretary
Government fee receipt or wire transfer confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the registered agent files an amended declaration or supplemental document within fourteen business days; failure to cure results in automatic withdrawal of the application without prejudice to re-application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA, Apia, Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon verification of the application, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation dated the filing date. Immediately thereafter, the registered agent opens the statutory registers (members, directors, officers, and charges), prepares share certificate number one for the initial subscriber, and issues the Certificate of Incumbency. The Company acquires separate legal personality on the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Register of Members and Register of Directors and Officers
Share certificate no. 1
Certificate of Incumbency prepared by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For clerical errors in the certificate, the registered agent files Form IC-6 to request reissuance at no additional government fee; substantive name corrections require a special resolution and re-registration with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Banking, and Payment-Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), licensed corporate service providers, and the Company's banking or payment-rail counterparties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notarize the corporate banking resolution and issue the certified incumbency package; open a corporate bank account and complete Stripe Billing or Wise onboarding using the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, and Certificate of Incumbency. File beneficial ownership records with the registered agent under SIFA AML/CFT record-keeping requirements and establish the annual SIFA license fee compliance calendar.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors
Bank account opening forms and KYC questionnaires
Light-touch AML/CFT internal control statement for the tax-exempt International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment processor queries economic substance or beneficial ownership, deliver the exemption certificate under Section 161 of the International Companies Act 1987 together with the registered agent's management services letter; resubmission within ten business days typically cures the query.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the International Company operates solely as a digital UI/UX design subscription agency (ISIC 7410) with no physical manufacturing or trading establishment in Samoa; therefore no industrial licensing board is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operational or manufacturing permit is required for digital design subscription services under Samoa law; the International Company is exempt from domestic business licensing under the International Companies Act 1987.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa — Environmental Assessment and Review Unit (not triggered).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based professional service generating no discharge, land disturbance, or emissions; no EIA registration is required under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 (Samoa).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial effluent, zero VOC emissions, and no regulated waste streams arise from remote UI/UX design subscription operations; no environmental compliance thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — the Company maintains no physical Samoan premises; its registered office is the professional suite of the licensed registered agent. If a future physical office lease in Apia is procured, fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority and a structural occupancy clearance would be required at that stage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (Matagaluega o Tupe Maua), Apia, Samoa; operating the Samoa Taxpayer Registration System and the Ministry for Revenue e-Services portal for taxpayer registration, filing, and compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity first incorporates an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 through the Samoa International Financial Services Centre (SIFSC) and the Registrar of Companies. Upon incorporation, the IC, acting through its licensed registered agent in Samoa, applies to the Ministry for Revenue for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) using the prescribed registration forms and supporting documents, which include the certificate of incorporation, charter and memorandum/articles of association, particulars of directors and shareholders, the registered agent's licence, and a declaration of offshore business activity. Registration is submitted via the Ministry's e-Services portal or a district revenue office; upon verification a TIN certificate is issued, and the entity is classified in the revenue system as a tax-exempt international company. The same TIN is used for all direct and indirect tax interactions, including any VAGST registration if the IC later makes taxable supplies in Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election, nor does it maintain hybrid mismatch election regimes applicable to international companies. Under the International Companies Act 1987, an IC is exempt by default from Samoan income tax and from Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) on offshore income and offshore transactions. The only statutory 'election' in practice is the voluntary surrender of International Company status, after which the entity becomes an ordinary domestic company under the Companies Act 2006 and falls within the normal Samoan tax net; no hybrid mismatch or pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 150,000 annual taxable turnover (compulsory registration threshold under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1991; voluntary registration may be permitted below the threshold, and offshore supplies by exempt international companies do not count toward the threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or government-authorised digital stamping regime is currently in force in Samoa. A VAGST-registered supplier must issue a compliant tax invoice within 28 days of supply, retain source records for audit, and file periodic VAGST returns through the Ministry for Revenue e-Services portal. API-based pre-clearance or real-time tax authority validation of invoices has not been implemented for the standard business environment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (VAGST at 0%) applies to: (a) goods physically exported from Samoa under a customs export declaration; (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not present in Samoa at the time of supply; and (c) certain international transport, freight, and directly related services. For the target International Company supplying UI/UX design-as-a-service subscriptions to non-resident clients, the offshore digital services qualify for zero-rating where the supplier has a Samoa VAGST registration and the place-of-supply rule is satisfied, or fall wholly outside Samoan VAGST where no Samoan nexus is established. International companies are presumptively exempt for offshore business activities, and a formal zero-rating claim is required only where the IC also makes taxable supplies in Samoa or elects to hold a VAGST registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs single-entry declaration / CusDec equivalent)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (carrier-issued proof of physical export, where goods are involved)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence of payment received from the non-resident customer
Commercial Invoice and VAGST Tax Invoice stating the zero-rated nature of the supply
Service Agreement / subscription contract evidencing the non-resident recipient and offshore place of supply
Client onboarding records confirming non-resident status and absence from Samoa at time of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may reassess zero-rated or exempt offshore supplies within the statutory limitation period and claw back VAGST together with late payment penalties (commonly 2% per month) and interest where the export trail is incomplete, the recipient is found to be Samoan-resident, or the place-of-supply test is failed. Claims supported by false documentation attract civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall for fraudulent or reckless behaviour, additional penalty-unit fines for failure to keep records under the Tax Administration Act 2012, and, where prosecuted, criminal fines and terms of imprisonment as prescribed for tax evasion. An International Company that breaches the offshore-declaration conditions also risks revocation of its SIFSC/international status and loss of the associated tax-exempt privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, which administers the Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1973; the CBS licenses authorized dealers (commercial banks) for all onshore foreign-exchange transactions and retains approval authority over capital-account movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed and only partially convertible currency. Current-account payments for trade in services are processed by authorized dealers on sight of underlying invoices and tax clearances, while capital-account transactions (equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend remittances) require CBS consent when routed through the onshore WST clearing system. The WS_IC, as a non-resident International Company earning design-subscription revenue abroad, can neutralize practical convertibility hurdles by holding perpetual USD receivables in an approved foreign-currency account at BSP Samoa and by avoiding WST conversion; profit remittance is then executed directly in USD via MT103 without CBS clearance, supported by the statutory income-tax exemption in the International Companies Act. Any incidental WST conversion for local expenses requires service invoices and an authorized-dealer declaration, with an approval lead time of roughly 3 to 7 business days.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1973, export receipts must generally be offered to an authorized dealer and converted into WST within one month of receipt unless CBS grants foreign-currency retention; current CBS practice permits retention of proceeds denominated in the same foreign currency as the underlying invoiced receivable, subject to periodic extension, and no mandatory percentage conversion applies to pure service exporters such as digital design subscription agencies. The surrender obligation is functionally inapplicable to the WS_IC because it is non-resident, tax-exempt, and earns foreign-source income settled entirely outside Samoa; retained USD collections never enter the onshore WST interbank market, and the entity should hold a standing retention exemption filed by its registered agent, supported by an annual non-resident attestation covering offshore board management, absence of local payroll, and offshore settlement patterns.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited (BSP) - Samoa operations, the largest commercial banking network in the jurisdiction and successor to the former ANZ Samoa retail and commercial franchise
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (USD/WST) for design-subscription collections, plus a separate Capital Escrow Account for contributed share capital and shareholder loans

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Current Account in WST and USD Foreign-Currency Account; escrow functionality available under separate arrangement

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Operating Account (WST/USD) used principally for domestic expense conversion and local contractor payroll support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with strict legal conditioning. Stripe does not maintain a Samoa-licensed settlement entity, and Wise Business does not offer WST-denominated local clearing, so both rails are usable only as auxiliary collection and payout layers. The WS_IC should contract Stripe_Billing through a Merchant of Record in a Stripe-supported jurisdiction (US, IE, or SG) acting as a disclosed agent, and Wise should be limited to sub-USD 5,000 contractor disbursements where the beneficiary holds a local payment rail. The EMI account must be in the name of the WS_IC, operated as a T+1 auto-sweep to the BSP Samoa USD operating account, staffed with no local employees, and restricted to non-Samoan-source counterparties to avoid creating a permanent establishment or foreign tax-residency nexus. Direct exclusive reliance on an offshore EMI as the principal depository is not viable because it would sever the correspondent clearing chain, trigger CRS/FATCA filing exposure in the EMI jurisdiction, and impair the registered agent's economic-substance attestation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoa's Tier-1 banks apply a hybrid physical-presence standard. BSP Samoa mandates initial in-person signing by one natural-person director or an authorized signatory before account opening, but permits remote participation for a second director via bank-accepted video call, provided the first director physically attends before the licensed registered agent in Apia and the agent performs real-time KYC verification with the bank's relationship manager. NBS and SCB generally require a physical meeting with a director or a locally appointed attorney-in-fact; a notarized Power of Attorney legalized by the Samoan Supreme Court is mandatory in that case. Purely remote onboarding with zero physical footprint is not available at any Samoa licensed bank; the total onboarding timeline should be planned at 10 to 20 business days, including registered-agent compliance, CBS sanctions screening, and the bank's AML committee sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-IC stigma: the bank automatically applies enhanced due diligence to an International Company because Samoa's offshore-company regime has been subject to repeated international monitoring, EU listing cycles, and FATF-style peer review, creating reputational risk for the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD Global Forum and EU listing status notes showing current compliance; CBS AML/CFT guidance letter; full beneficial-ownership declaration down to every natural person with 10% or more; corporate organization chart showing the WS_IC as a single-purpose design-subsidiary; audited or independent-accountant-reviewed financial statements; and a compliance certificate from the licensed registered agent confirming that annual government fees, corporate registers, and economic-substance filings are current.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency and economic-substance ambiguity: the bank must determine whether the IC is actually managed and controlled from Samoa and therefore no longer qualifies as non-resident and tax-exempt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written legal opinion from a Samoa-licensed attorney confirming the International Companies Act tax exemption and the non-resident election; certified board minutes showing all management decisions taken outside Samoa; absence of Samoan employees, leases, or immovable property; CRS self-certification showing no Samoa tax residence; and a management-services agreement limiting the registered agent to administrative duties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds from digital design subscriptions that arrive as automated Stripe/Wise settlements without a visible client-contract trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed design-subscription agreements (MSA and SOW) with named international clients; rolling invoice register mapped to Stripe_Billing settlement reports; web-domain and portfolio IP-ownership records; a bank reference letter from the settlement EMI covering the prior 12 months; and wire-traceable client payment reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure arising from a remote, globally diverse client base that the bank cannot independently assess.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence reports for every client with annual contract value above USD 25,000; real-time sanctions screening of clients and payees; PEP declarations from all directors, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories; a board policy limiting clients to non-sanctioned OECD and Pacific-territory counterparties; and a legal representation letter confirming no listed person receives economic benefit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS misclassification of the entity and its beneficial owners, which would expose the bank to cross-border reporting failures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity-level W-8BEN-E submitted to BSP Samoa; W-9 or W-8BEN collected from every beneficial owner; a written representation that no US person is a shareholder; CRS reportable-jurisdiction schedule with full TINs of all ultimate natural persons; and an undertaking to update FATCA/CRS forms on any ownership change.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans enter via standard SWIFT MT103 from the remitting group bank to the WS_IC's BSP Samoa USD account. The wire must carry unambiguous purpose text reading 'Equity contribution - share capital subscription' or 'Non-resident shareholder loan disbursement'; the receiving bank requires allotment board resolutions and a share-register extract for equity, and an executed intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest, term, and amortization schedule for debt. If retained in USD and held in a foreign-currency account, an injection requires no CBS consent; any conversion to WST for onshore spending triggers the authorized dealer's CBS exchange-control application using the same purpose classification. Onboarding must be supported by the remitting bank's source-of-funds letter, beneficial-owner declarations, and a capital verification certificate from the registered agent once aggregate injections exceed USD 100,000; the Capital Escrow Account should be used only for injections pending their formal designation as operating equity or intercompany debt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing hierarchy for WS_IC operating payments: (1) SWIFT MT103 wires from the BSP Samoa USD operating account for all vendor and contractor payments above USD 5,000, with purpose description 'Fees for professional and technical services - other business services (ISIC 7410)' and invoice number cited; (2) Wise Business batch API for payments below USD 5,000 where the contractor holds EUR, GBP, AUD, or JPY local rails and cost efficiency outweighs SWIFT traceability; (3) Stripe_Billing acts solely as the subscription collection and Merchant-of-Record interface, with settlement flowing to a designated supported-jurisdiction virtual account and then daily sweeping to BSP Samoa USD; (4) commercial Letters of Credit are not required for design-subscription services, although a standby LC issued by BSP Samoa may be furnished to enterprise clients as a performance guarantee when contract values exceed USD 250,000; and (5) all disbursements must be backed by contractor agreements and CBS anti-money-laundering declarations for any single outgoing transfer above USD 50,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/WST forward contracts (tenors up to 12 months) available from BSP Samoa with a documented underlying design-service receivable or payable exposure.
Non-deliverable USD/WST forward (NDF) overlay executed offshore when onshore authorized-dealer limits or documentary requirements make a deliverable forward impractical.
Multi-currency account netting: maintaining USD as the primary settlement currency and WST only for domestic expense tranches to minimize forced conversions and eliminate repeated bid-ask spreads.
Simple cross-currency swap between WST and USD where a WST component exists in an intercompany loan; practical market depth in Samoa is thin and CBS notification is required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the anniversary date of incorporation; grace period of 30 calendar days after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late sanction of USD 20 per day up to USD 600; if unpaid by the end of the 6 months following the anniversary, the Registrar may strike the company off and forfeit its assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) and the registered agent's AML compliance file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Furnished with the renewal filing within 30 days after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of the certificate causes the registered agent to cease to act; the company is treated as not having a Samoan agent and may be struck off at the Registrar's discretion.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for International Companies unless the company is licensed as a bank, insurance, or estate management business, or unless holders of at least 10% of issued voting shares serve a written requisition; otherwise an internal voluntary review suffices.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed local GAAP for International Companies; IFRS may be adopted voluntarily; books may be kept in any currency but must fairly disclose financial position and permit accurate statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At every share transfer, the member register and beneficial ownership record must be updated in the registered office within 14 days; on each annual renewal, the registered agent must confirm in the Compliance Certificate that the UBO schedule is current and that no undisclosed control has arisen. Missing UBO information blocks renewal.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 4,000, only if shareholder requisition occurs; otherwise zero

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (Samoa resident ordinary companies, Income Tax Act 2012)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Company (IC) statutory exemption: 0% corporate income tax for 20 years from incorporation (extendable) on all income other than income derived from sources in Samoa; no capital gains tax; no dividend withholding tax on IC distributions; annual government fee is the sole revenue charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form IR-IC/AR) filed with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), via the Samoa International Companies online registry.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the IC's incorporation date each year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered IC name and registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert exact certificate name; any trade name in the design subscription business must be declared as an alternate name.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and registered agent in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed Samoa registered agent must be appointed and countersign; correspondence address of the beneficial owner may be included for service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders are permitted; provide full legal names, nationalities, and residential addresses for the beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of non-carrying-on-business in Samoa and absence of Samoan-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC must confirm it has not derived income from sources within Samoa and is not carrying on trade or business in Samoa; subscription income from foreign clients routed through Stripe Billing or Wise is reported as non-Samoan source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee schedule and payment confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must ensure the registered agent remits the annual fee before the anniversary date to avoid late penalties and strike-off.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of up to WST 200 per month; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers automatic strike-off; restoration fee of WST 300 plus all outstanding annual fees and penalties; trading while struck off is an offence punishable by fine and director liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Samoa Inland Revenue corporate return) filed through the Samoa Inland Revenue electronic filing portal, applicable only where an IC inadvertently derives Samoan-source income or is re-characterized as carrying on business in Samoa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year (which may be a substituted accounting period approved by the Commissioner).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income from all sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident and tax-exempt ICs report only Samoan-source gross income; offshore UI/UX design subscription revenue is excluded and separately disclosed as exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income and International Company statutory exclusion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the IC exemption under the International Companies Act 2007 for all non-Samoan-source active business income; maintain client contracts, payment logs from Stripe Billing and Wise, and service delivery records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions and expenses properly incurred in producing assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deductions directly attributable to any Samoan-source income are allowable; no deduction may be claimed for offshore design team costs unless the IC is assessed as carrying on business in Samoa.
Nil for a compliant tax-exempt IC; if non-compliant, enter the net amount and apply the 27% corporate rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 27% less final withholding tax credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty credits only where a Samoa DTA applies and a valid Samoa tax residency certificate is held.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Finalize payment through the Samoa Inland Revenue portal; any refund is subject to audit and proof of source documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for each month or part of a month, up to a maximum of 100%; further late payment interest at the prescribed statutory rate; criminal fines for inaccurate or fraudulent returns up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an International Company (statutorily exempt under the International Companies Act 2007); the general Samoa domestic dividend withholding tax rate for ordinary resident companies is 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain a Samoa tax residency certificate from Samoa Inland Revenue, (2) complete the applicable withholding tax reduction declaration form and submit it, with the DTA article citation, to the paying IC or its registered agent, (3) provide Samoa tax identification number and evidence of beneficial ownership, and (4) if excess WHT was applied at source, lodge a refund claim with Samoa Inland Revenue within the statutory time limit. Samoa maintains an active DTA network including treaties with New Zealand, Australia, China, and others; the specific treaty must be confirmed before reliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 10% final withholding tax on interest and 10% on royalties paid to non-residents; applicable DTA rates generally cap at 10%, with certain treaties providing 0% for interest paid to another treaty state's government or to the beneficial owner of the interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory local-file threshold specific to International Companies has been gazetted; the arm's length standard applies to all related-party cross-border transactions. Prudent administrative threshold: maintain a contemporaneous Local File where annual related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000, and prepare a Master File where the worldwide group's consolidated turnover exceeds WST 100,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies Act 2007, as amended by Samoa's economic substance legislation, requires every IC to maintain a registered agent, registered office, accounting records, and an adequate economic presence appropriate to its activities. ICs carrying on enumerated 'relevant activities' — including banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing, leasing, headquarters, IP holding, distribution, and service centres — must demonstrate real substance in Samoa through physical premises, locally engaged employees, and core decision-making in Samoa. A pure UI/UX design subscription agency (ISIC 7410 / NAICS 541430) with foreign clients and no Samoan-source income is not an enumerated relevant activity; however, the IC must avoid holding passive IP or intangibles that could be recharacterized as an IP holding business and must maintain tangible commercial substance commensurate with its design-as-a-service functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Filing (Income Tax Act 2012)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or understating Samoan-source income, fabricating foreign client contracts, backdating invoices, or using the IC to disguise a trade actually carried on in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded plus statutory interest; criminal liability: fine up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years; forfeiture of proceeds under asset recovery powers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorize false filings are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax, penalties, and interest; the corporate veil is pierced for knowing participation; the court may impose personal bankruptcy, departure prohibition orders, and extradition for serious tax crime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Sham Substance (General Anti-Avoidance Rule and International Companies Act 2007)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating an IC with no real commercial substance, using nominee shareholders, mischaracterizing Samoan services as offshore subscription revenue, or artificially alienating income away from the actual service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of the arrangement under Samoa's general anti-avoidance rule, voiding the IC tax exemption; reassessment of profits at 27% with penalties up to 200%; strike-off of the IC; fines for false declarations under the International Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered agents who certify false substance declarations are personally liable for the resulting tax liability, restitution of diverted profits, disqualification as company officers, and potential imprisonment for fraud; travel bans may be imposed pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Financial Sanctions Breach (Samoa AML/CFT Act 2018 and International Companies Act Beneficial Ownership Regime)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misuse of the IC for money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, converting illicit proceeds through Stripe Billing or Wise payout rails, or failing to maintain the beneficial ownership register and report suspicious transactions to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to WST 500,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years; freezing of corporate assets; revocation of the IC registration; prohibition from using the Samoan financial system; regulatory fines against the registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and compliance personnel who knowingly participate, facilitate, or fail to report are personally subject to criminal conviction, confiscation of benefits, travel bans, and extradition risk; the corporate veil is disregarded for deliberate AML violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Annual Return and Annual Fee Non-Compliance; Trading While Struck Off (International Companies Act 2007)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the IC annual return, failure to pay the annual government fee, continued trading after compulsory strike-off, or failure to disclose a change of directors, shareholders, or registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compounding late fees, automatic strike-off from the Register, restoration fee of WST 300 plus all arrears; trading while struck off is a statutory offence attracting fines; each transaction in a struck-off IC is invalid for tax exemption purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who trade through a struck-off IC are jointly and severally liable for all debts and contractual obligations incurred during the struck-off period; the court may order restitution to third-party creditors, impose disqualification orders, and issue travel bans to compel restitution.
